story: On Sunday evening at 6:17, with the October sun still warm at 78 degrees, Gary is sketching wiring and speaker layouts at his workbench for the cart lights and sound system he wants to show Hal and the board. Donna, cheerful as ever, is out on Magnolia Loop asking Hal to look over her hospital-themed cart plans, with her three bandaged flamingos, before they go to Architectural Review. Hal, gruff but content, has his heart set on hauling a folding table and chairs to dinner, but Rosa, determined to keep the peace, waves him off the notebook and insists he come eat before Donna's casserole goes cold.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Draw up a careful wiring and speaker layout sketch for the cart lights and sound system to show Hal and the board

gary.thought_process: I'm home, alone, and it's a nice evening. My Architectural Review application is already filed (Tick 156), and I told myself I'd keep the cart in the garage until it's approved, so I shouldn't be adding visible exterior mods to the cart on the street. Hal said he'd sign off on my sketches, and Rosa and Donna are all pushing the 'plans first' approach. The legal thing to do is get the wiring and sound system plan sketched out on paper at the workbench, with the lights and speaker layout, so it's ready to show Hal and the board. That keeps me busy, useful, and within L-01. Sound testing can wait until it's approved and well before quiet hours anyway.

parameters.content: Draw up a careful wiring and speaker layout sketch for the cart lights and sound system to show Hal and the board

donna.thought_process: Rosa just pinned her hospital theme sketch and Hal is standing right here with his rule-book eye. Gary has gone home to sketch the carts, so the committee needs someone to keep the flamingo plans legal. Hal already warned Gary about L-01 and the three-ornament limit, and I want our Halloween carts to win fair and square. If I get Hal on record that bandaged flamingos still count toward three, nobody can complain later. I haven't said anything this tick, so a light, friendly line to Hal keeps goodwill up and moves the parade plan forward.

parameters.content: Hal, I love the hospital theme and I'm keeping my flamingos to three, bandages and all. If I swing by with my cart plans tomorrow, will you look them over before I send them to Architectural Review?

hal.thought_process: Gary's gone home to sort out his sketches, and Donna and Rosa have already pinned up their notices about Architectural Review, ornaments at three, and dinner. The street is in good order. Rosa's dinner is tonight, so I'll offer to carry something over. It gives me a reason to be useful and keeps me near the plans. Don't repeat the cart lecture. Move things forward.

parameters.content: Saw your notice, Rosa. Sound rules, and I'll hold Gary to every one of them. What time is dinner, and what can I haul over? I'll bring the folding table, and I know where the extra chairs are.

rosa.thought_process: Donna and Hal are both right here on Magnolia Loop, and my goal is to get all three neighbors at my welcome dinner table. Gary already came by, and I haven't actually pinned Hal down yet. He's been all notebook and rules, so I'll keep it warm and plain: tell him there's a seat for him and food on the table, and the rules can wait. It's 6:17, dinner is happening now, so a direct invitation beats another round of parade talk.

parameters.content: Hal, I appreciate the rundown, and I'll keep every cart inside the rules. But right now there's a plate with your name on it at my table, and Donna's casserole is going cold. Leave the notebook on the porch and come eat with us.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
